title: WPMS/208/2010 of M/S NARAYAN CREATIONS P LIMITED Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
WPMS No. 208 of 2010
Hon'ble Tarun Agarwala, J.
Mr. Manish Goyal, Advocate assisted by
Mr. B.N. Molakhi, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Vipul Sharma, Advocate for the
respondents.
The petitioner applied for an industrial
plot which was granted and a lease deed was
executed on 18th April, 2006. Under this lease, a
period of nine months was given to start the
construction and two years to complete the
construction. In paragraph 2(J) of the petition,
the petitioner contends that the possession of the
land, in question, was handed over to the
petitioner on 29th July, 2006. In paragraph 2(M),
it was further stated that without serving a notice
of 60 days as stipulated in the lease deed, the
respondent cancelled the lease deed by an order
dated 18th January, 2008 and forfeited the
deposit without issuing a notice and without
giving an opportunity of hearing. The petitioner,
being aggrieved by the said order, has filed the
present writ petition.
The State Industrial Development
Corporation of Uttarakhand Limited (SIDCUL)
respondent No. 2 has filed a counter affidavit.
The fact that possession was given to the
petitioner after the execution of the sale deed on

29.07.2006 has not been disputed by the
respondent in paragraph 22 of the counter
affidavit. In paragraph 25 of the counter
affidavit, it has been alleged that the lease deed
was cancelled since commercial production was
not started within two years from the date of the
allotment and that the notice for cancellation
was served to the petitioner on 8th June, 2006
and 7th July, 2006.
In the opinion of the Court, the notice for
cancellation as per the said notice was patently
misconceived, inasmuch as, possession
admittedly was given to the petitioner on 29th
July, 2006 and the plan for construction was
sanctioned on 25th July, 2006. Further, the
respondent in paragraph 25 of the counter
affidavit does not deny that no opportunity of
hearing was provided to the petitioner.
In the light of the aforesaid, the impugned
order cancelling the lease deed is patently
illegal, arbitrary and violative of the principle of
natural justice and cannot be sustained. The
impugned orders are quashed. The writ petition
is allowed. It would be open to the respondent to
pass a fresh order in accordance with law.
(Tarun Agarwala, J.)
Dated 03.01.2012
Shiv
